lines.text: I ranked 6 tools for building a trading strategy from S to F, so you don't have to.
Quant trading just means trading with rules and data instead of your gut.
And yes, I am biased because we built one.
Asking chat GPT what to buy.
F tier.
You're just getting an opinion that nobody has actually tested.
Excel.
D tier.
You can test a strategy on past prices in a spreadsheet, but one wrong sell and your test is secretly using tomorrow's price to make today's trade.
Your results look amazing, but they're fake.
Meta trader.
C tier.
It's popular for Forex, which is trading currencies like the dollar and the euro.
But to build a bot that trades for you, it needs to learn its own coding language.
Trading view.
B tier.
Really good charts and it can test strategies on past prices.
But to do that, you need to learn its coding language.
Pinescript.
Quant connect.
A tier.
Very powerful for testing strategies, but you have to write real code in Python or C-sharp.
Notice the pattern?
Everything from C to A wants you to be a programmer.
Cube.
S tier.
You describe the idea in plain English.
It turns it into exact rules, tests them on past prices and runs it.
No code required.
The hard part of trading should be the idea, not learning how to code.
Disagree?
Drop your tier list in the comments or comment cube and I'll send you the full breakdown.

notes: **Format source:** our own M05 · https://www.instagram.com/reel/DerwxsIzyeX/ · copy its rhythm: one app every 4–5s here (fewer words than M05), each app = name → tier word on its own ("F tier.") → one line with "but"; the board fills one row on the tier word; one 2–3s homepage insert per app; the board drops in on "so you don't have to".

**Layout:** M05's. Mark full frame, the tier board (A2) fixed in the top third (1080×640) and filling F → S. Homepage inserts replace the board in the top third for 2–3s, then the board comes back. Captions 2–4 words, M05's style ("TQX Captions" preset, key word on the navy highlight box), chest height (y = 1380).
**Times** are estimates at Mark's pace (3.0 words a second, about 52s, 155 words). Re-time to the real take.

notes: **Presenter:** Mark. One person, one list, in video order.

**Before recording:** every homepage is recorded logged out, Chrome full screen, zoom 125%, no tabs or bookmarks showing, cookie banners closed with "Reject" or "Necessary only". Qube on Mark's own login, notifications off. No emails, keys or account names on screen.

**Reuse from M05:** the tier board, the big-text style and the caption style. Duplicate them from the M05 CapCut project and swap only the logos and names. If it isn't available, build from the specs below.

rows.how: 1. Laptop camera or phone vertical (9:16), eye level, lock focus and exposure, M05 framing. 2. Head and chest in the lower two thirds; top third (640px) clear for the board. 3. Record the hook twice, clean. 4. Record lines 1–10 in one take, fast, no pauses. Say each tier word on its own with a short beat after it: "F tier." "D tier." 5. Move in close and record three times: "Here's the line. Below it, you're running their strategy. Above it, you're testing your own."

1. Get each logo from the company's own press or brand page: Cryptohopper, 3Commas, Trade Ideas, TrendSpider, Composer. 2. (Inter Bold 48px). 3. **CHECK: Qube's logo is not in this frame;** it shows for the first time on the S hit (A2 state 6, logo from the TQX team). 4. Export PNG.

Chips, Inter Bold 28px #0B0F14 on gold #E8B04B, 16px rounded, right end of the row, text exactly: "THEIR STRATEGY", "PRESET", "AI'S CALLS". One PNG each. 4. rows.what: Qube: strategy typed → backtest → every trade
rows.how: 1. Chrome, full screen, zoom 125%, https://www.tqx.ai logged in, open Qube, new strategy. 2. Start a screen recording. 3. Type exactly, by hand, don't paste: `Buy the S&P 500 when it drops 2% in a day. Sell once it's up 2% from where I bought, or if it falls another 3%.` 4. Build, then press Backtest. 5. Hold 3s on the result. 6. Open the list of every trade and scroll top to bottom in about 4s, so losing trades (red) are visible. Hold 2s. Stop. 7. Screenshot the result and the trade list. 8. Go back, open one of the ready-made Hong Kong stock strategies, press Backtest, and record 3s of its result (for "US and Hong Kong prices"). **CHECK: if no Hong Kong strategy is in the list, tell Mark before the edit; line 9 depends on it.** **CHECK: the trade list shows at least one losing trade; if it shows none, tell Mark before the edit (line 9 says "losers too").** **CHECK: test period is five years or less. Don't change any number Qube shows; none is spoken.**
